newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas creeps higher, stock refills continue.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas creeps higher, stock refills continue.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly higher Friday as storage replenishment continued to support the market, though some late selling tempered the overall increase in price, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices rose an average of two cents to about $2.12-2.18 per mmBtu, with the lower-priced deals reported done shortly before nomination deadlines.
Henry Hub was quoted at $2.17-2.22, while Transco (Station 65) hovered around $2.18-2.21.
Cash continued to mirror NYMEX as July Henry Hub gas futures ranged from $2.165 to $2.214 in Friday's session.
Similarly in west Texas, Permian prices gained about two cents to about $1.97-1.99, while Waha values were quoted at $2.05-2.08.

Southern California prices, however, slipped five cents to about $2.10 in anticipation of a weaker demand this weekend and temperature highs in Los Angeles only in the low-80s F, according to Weather Services Corp (WSC).
In the Midwest, prices rose three cents to about $2.03-2.05, with Chicago city-gate quoted at $2.23.
At the Detroit city-gate, gas sold at $2.32-2.35.
In the East, New York city gate prices climbed into the high-$2.30s to about $2.40 as temperatures were expected to moderate to slightly above normal by the middle of next week, according to WSC.

Also lending some support to the market, traders said, was the uncertainty surrounding testing in Vermilion Bay, offshore Louisiana. The U.S. Coast Guard on Thursday ordered several lines shut for testing after small bubbles were spotted in the water.
